key_insight: Scaling self-supervised pretraining with a large, curated surgical video corpus (10,535 videos, 214.5M frames) and a reproducible recipe (SurgRec-MAE and SurgRec-JEPA) produces stronger, generalizable surgical foundation models.
problem_solved: Addresses limited data scale, low procedural diversity, and inconsistent evaluation in surgical video pretraining by providing a large multi-source dataset and a reproducible training/evaluation pipeline.
method: Curate a multi-source surgical video corpus of 10,535 videos (214.5M frames) to increase scale and procedural diversity.
Design reproducible self-supervised pretraining recipes instantiated as SurgRec-MAE (masked autoencoding) and SurgRec-JEPA (joint embedding predictive architecture).
Provide a standardized training and evaluation pipeline to enable fair comparisons and easier downstream fine-tuning.
impact: Makes it practical for AI/ML practitioners to pretrain and transfer robust surgical video models at scale, improving performance on downstream tasks (phase recognition, tool detection, skill assessment) while enabling reproducible research and benchmarking.
visual_elements: Dataset-scale infographic: stacked bars or icon grid showing 10,535 videos and 214.5M frames across sources/procedures.
Pipeline flowchart: data curation → SurgRec-MAE / SurgRec-JEPA pretraining → standardized evaluation → downstream tasks.
Architecture comparison: side-by-side schematic of MAE vs JEPA objectives and training signals.
Benchmark chart: before/after or multi-task bar chart showing gains on key surgical downstream tasks.
paper_title: Scaling Video Pretraining for Surgical Foundation Models
paper_authors: Sicheng Lu, Zikai Xiao, Jianhui Wei, Danyu Sun, Qi Lu
